examples.solution_text:
(a) Collect like terms first, then subtract $2x$ from both sides.
$\begin{align*}9x+11-4x&=2x+24\\5x+11&=2x+24\\3x+11&=24\\3x&=13\\x&=\frac{13}{3}\end{align*}$
(b) Add $4y$ to both sides to keep the remaining coefficient positive.
$\begin{align*}-4y-8&=3y+11\\-8&=7y+11\\-19&=7y\\y&=-\frac{19}{7}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
(a) A student expands $-3(4x+7)$ as $-12x+21$. Explain the mistake, then solve $-3(4x+7)+11=5x-8$.
(b) Solve $4(5w-7)=3(2w+11)$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The $-3$ multiplies both terms, so $-3\times7=-21$, not $21$.
$\begin{align*}-3(4x+7)+11&=5x-8\\-12x-21+11&=5x-8\\-12x-10&=5x-8\\-10&=17x-8\\-2&=17x\\x&=-\frac{2}{17}\end{align*}$
(b) Expand both brackets, then move the pronumerals to one side.
$\begin{align*}4(5w-7)&=3(2w+11)\\20w-28&=6w+33\\14w-28&=33\\14w&=61\\w&=\frac{61}{14}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Solve:
(a) $7(3t+8)=91$ by dividing both sides by $7$ first.
(b) $7(3t+8)=67$ by expanding first.
Explain why expanding first is useful in (b).
examples.solution_text:
(a) Divide both sides by $7$.
$\begin{align*}7(3t+8)&=91\\3t+8&=13\\3t&=5\\t&=\frac{5}{3}\end{align*}$
(b) Expand the brackets first.
$\begin{align*}7(3t+8)&=67\\21t+56&=67\\21t&=11\\t&=\frac{11}{21}\end{align*}$
In (b), dividing $67$ by $7$ would introduce a fraction straight away. Expanding first keeps whole numbers in the working until the final division.

(a) Expand, then simplify and use inverse operations.
$\begin{align*}-3(z+4)-2&=10\\-3z-12-2&=10\\-3z-14&=10\\-3z&=24\\z&=-8\end{align*}$
(b) Expand, then collect like terms before solving.
$\begin{align*}4(2u-3)-3u&=18\\8u-12-3u&=18\\5u-12&=18\\5u&=30\\u&=6\end{align*}$
